# dsh-account-model-hub (fork of dsh-plugin-subscriptions) [](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)
English | 中文
## Settings layout
The settings page now has two top-level views in the same plugin:

- **Accounts & Quota**: sign in/out providers, API keys, quota cards, account pool and usage.
- **Mo
del settings**: per-provider model visibility, default reasoning effort, display name, context and p
rovider tools. Each provider card opens a model-only editor, so these controls are no longer buried
inside account management.

## Platform support
The plugin is plain JavaScript/TypeScript with no native dependencies or OS-restricted packages. It
uses DSH home paths, `node:path`, and `node:os` throughout; Claude Code credential import has an exp
licit macOS Keychain branch (`/usr/bin/security`) and a file fallback; OAuth callbacks and media fil
es are platform-neutral.

- Windows: tested.
- macOS: expected to work with the same DSH version; Claude Code import uses Keyc
hain, other providers use the same browser OAuth/device-code flows. No macOS smoke test has been rec

orded yet.
- Linux: expected to work with file-based Claude credentials; OAuth/browser flows are the

yet.
- Linux: expected to work with file-based Claude credentials; OAuth/browser flows are the same.
For an open-source release, add a macOS/Linux smoke test to the release checklist: install → login C
odex/Claude → open both settings views → verify quota footer → run one model call.
This fork keeps the upstream subscription providers and adds a first-class **OpenCode Go** line (API
-key accounts, three upstream protocols, account pool and per-account 5h/weekly/monthly quota). See
docs/opencode-go.md and NOTICE.
Use your **ChatGPT (Codex)**, **Claude**, **Grok (X Premium)**, **GitHub Copilot**, **Google Antigra
vity** and **OpenCode Go** accounts in DeepSeek Harness — no API keys for the OAuth subscriptions. C
odex, Grok, and Antigravity log in via OAuth in the dsh web UI (Settings → Accounts & Quota), while
Copilot uses the GitHub OAuth device flow; Claude imports credentials from an existing Claude Code s
ession when there is one (macOS Keychain or `~/.claude/.credentials.json`) and otherwise falls back
to the same browser OAuth flow, so the Claude Code CLI is not required. Tokens live at `~/.dsh/plugi
ns/account-hub/auth.json` (mode 0600) and refresh automatically.
## Subscription and model display names
Open **Settings → Accounts & Quota → Manage** to set a subscription display name, or edit a model's
display name under **Edit model list**. Both share the existing Save/Cancel actions; clearing a name
or choosing Reset to default and saving restores the original name. Names are single-line text of u
p to 80 characters, stored per provider and model ID in `provider-settings.json`, and survive restar
ts and catalog refreshes. They only change presentation: provider IDs, model IDs, reasoning settings
, and account routing remain unchanged. Existing account aliases continue to work independently.
Subscription display names also label provider groups in the native model picker. Saving a cleared n
ame restores the provider's default group title.

### DSH compatibility
Version `0.9.7` added support for DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`; DSH `0.2.1-alpha.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.3` and `0.2.1-
rc.2` are supported as well, with development dependencies pinned to `0.2.1-rc.2`. It handles reques
t-only messages, first-class tool results, preparing tool views, and offloaded image placeholders wh
ile retaining legacy history translation. `0.2.1-rc.2` additionally requires tool arguments on every
call head and takes the web runtime's provider overrides as `Volatile` refs. Other `0.2` prerelease
s are not implicitly allowed.
In DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`, the load-time check uses `engines.dsh` when declared; otherwise, every `@deepse
ek-ai/dsh` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer must match the running DSH version. Prereleases participate
in this check. This plugin does not declare `engines.dsh`, so its DSH peer ranges determine whether
it can load. The `@deepseek-ai/cordis` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` peers affect package-manager
dependency resolution, not this load-time check. They keep their `^4.0.1` / `^3.18.1` floors and als
o list the `4.0.5-alpha` / `3.18.5-alpha` builds bundled with DSH `0.2.1-alpha.2` and `0.2.1-alpha.3
`, because those caret ranges exclude these prereleases under npm's default semver rules.
The current release supports the published DSH `0.1.1-rc.2`, `0.1.2-alpha`/`rc`, `0.1.3-alpha`, `0.1
.5-alpha`/`rc`, and `0.1.7-rc` lines, including `0.1.5-rc.2` and `0.1.7-rc.2`. The `0.1.5-alpha.1` p
eer-range anchor intentionally covers the later `0.1.5-alpha`, `0.1.5-rc`, and stable `0.1.5` builds
under npm semver rules; the `0.1.7-rc.1` anchor likewise covers the later `0.1.7-rc` and stable `0.
1.7` builds. DSH `0.1.6-alpha` and `0.1.7-alpha` are not included until they have been separately ve
ilds. DSH `0.1.6-alpha` and `0.1.7-alpha` are not included until they have been separately verified.
